core_obligations: Reductio set-up (proof lines 780-785): suppose an isomorphism f : A -> A_a exists; A_a is a proper subset, so f moves something; take the least b with b != f(b).
Forward comparison (lines 788-790): x < b forces x = f(x) by minimality, and f preserves order, so x < f(b).
Backward comparison (lines 791-793): x < f(b) forces f-inverse(x) < b, hence f-inverse(x) = x and x < b.
Finish (line 786 statement inside the set-up): the two strict lower sets agree, extensionality gives b = f(b), contradicting the reductio choice of b.
proof_roadmap: Assume an isomorphism onto a proper initial segment.
Pick the least point where it moves something.
Show below-b and below-f(b) define the same initial region in both directions.
Conclude b = f(b) by extensionality, contradiction.
